title: A SEO Manager’s Playbook to Unmasking Competitor Mentions
summary: Every time ChatGPT, Gemini, or Google AI Overviews answers a buyer’s question, they hand a shortlist of brands a seal of unearned trust.
body_text: Introduction Every time ChatGPT, Gemini, or Google AI Overviews answers a buyer’s question, they hand a shortlist of brands a seal of unearned trust. Your competitors are either on that list right now or fighting to get there. Traditional rank monitoring is blind to this. Generative engine results synthesize answers from probabilistic models, not crawled indexes. A competitor cited in an AI-generated answer captures mindshare inside a conversation you cannot see unless you go looking for it. This guide lays out the tooling, metrics, and execution framework to turn invisible AI citations into a structured competitive intelligence stream. Key Takeaways Competitor citation intelligence is the new rank tracking. Here is what the framework below will walk you through. Core tools and real pricing: Dedicated platforms range from $29/mo (Otterly) to $99/mo (Semrush, Profound) with Naridon adding automated fixes at $49 /mo. The metric set that matters: Track mention frequency, citation link detection, sentiment score, and average position to measure competitive standing. Prompt-specific monitoring beats broad scanning: You gain use by monitoring the exact commercial and comparison queries where deals are won or lost. Verification is mandatory: AI outputs are non-deterministic. Live browsing and cross-referencing separate hallucinated citations from genuine wins. Hidden labor is the silent budget killer: Tools that stop at analytics push $500 to $1,500/month in manual implementation costs back onto your team. Translate gaps into revenue: Use citation intelligence to prioritize content creation, build source authority, and shift share of AI voice into measurable traffic. Step 1: Understand the Battlefield, Generative Engine Results vs. Traditional Search A generative answer is not a list of links. The engine builds a unique, synthetic response on the fly, pulling from training data and live retrieval. It varies every time it runs. Traditional search retrieves and ranks webpages. Generative engines compose a one-off reply for each query. Hand ten people the same prompt, and the outputs can diverge wildly. Generative answers usually surface a smaller, variable set of sources than a traditional results page. An SEO manager who treats generative monitoring like a weekly rank report chases noise and misses the signal. Citation dynamics also work differently. A blue link earns a click only when the user taps it. An AI-generated answer positions the cited brand as the answer itself. That citation carries weight because the AI platform staked its credibility on it. AI visibility measures how often AI platforms like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity mention your brand when they answer questions. The practical threat: a competitor invisible on page one can still dominate the generative answer, piling up unearned trust that traditional SEO tools cannot detect. Step 2: Build Your Competitor Intelligence Toolkit, Tools, Pricing, and Features A growing set of platforms now tracks whether ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and other LLMs cite your brand when they answer questions. Most monitor between four and eight AI engines depending on tier. Semrush’s AI Visibility Toolkit starts at $99/month and bundles domain-level competitor reports, custom prompt daily monitoring, and sentiment analysis. It covers Google AI Overviews, Gemini, ChatGPT, and Perplexity alongside a broader SEO suite. For teams that want lighter weight and low cost, Otterly starts at $29/month. Its monitoring spans ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Microsoft Copilot, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, and Gemini. It also detects when AI platforms cite your content with links, showing the cited page and analyzing which content is earning visibility, though Claude, Gemini, and Google AI Mode require paid add-ons. Profound positions differently. Its starter tier is $499/month, analytics only, tracking four AI engines. No tier includes automated fixes: at any price point, you're receiving analytics and recommendations that require manual implementation. Naridon addresses that gap directly. It starts at $49 /mo with no hidden fees and includes automated fixes that other tools charge $500+/mo for (or don't offer at all). Its $49/mo entry tier already covers eight engines, more than Profound’s four-engine $499/mo floor. The pricing spread creates a sharp trade-off decision. Analytics-only tools load a hidden labor line onto your P&L. Manual implementation of their recommendations typically adds $500 to $1,500/month in hidden labor costs. For a marketing team running five-figure monthly SEO retainers, a read-only platform that does not execute changes becomes a reporting cost rather than an optimization engine. You can use a platform like Siftly to benchmark competitor mentions and track AI-referred clicks without the manual overhead, structuring competitive intelligence as a continuous feed rather than a periodic report. The right stack will depend on whether your priority is broad SEO integration or a dedicated GEO workflow where automated fixes accelerate the feedback loop. Step 3: Define Your Monitoring Metrics, What to Track and Why Raw citation counts are not a KPI. They are input material. You need metrics that connect to competitive positioning and revenue risk. Start with brand mention frequency. A mention means the AI platform named your brand in its response; a citation means it linked to your website as a source. Track both, for your brand and your top competitors. When mention count rises but citation links stay flat, you have a trust gap: the AI knows your name but will not stake its credibility on your content. Citation link detection comes next. A link to a competitor's content is a direct endorsement. Map which pages earn citations across your query clusters. If a competitor's pricing comparison page keeps getting cited for commercial prompts, your own content strategy has to answer for that. Sentiment score and average position round out the picture. Sentiment captures whether an AI answer frames a competitor as the recommended choice, a viable alternative, or a cautionary example. You can benchmark this across engines. Siftly tracks how often your brand appears in AI-generated responses and visualizes its standing against competitors. Average position ranks brands ordinally inside a generative answer, showing who the AI treats as category leader. Step 4: Execute Prompt-Specific Monitoring, Capture the Exact Queries Broad monitoring tells you which direction the wind is blowing. Prompt-specific monitoring tells you exactly which competitors are taking your customers. AI citations come from three query types. Commercial intent prompts (“best Shopify SEO tools”) have someone ready to buy. If your competitor gets cited as the top pick, that revenue walks out the door. Comparison prompts (“Shopify SEO tool vs. alternative”) hand a competitor implied superiority with nothing more than a mention. Then there are informational prompts (“how to optimize Shopify product pages”) where the AI embeds a tool recommendation inside a how-to answer. The reader came for advice and left with your competitor’s name. The table below sorts each prompt type by its threat level, how often to monitor it, and what to do with what you find. Prompt Category Example Query Why It Threatens You Monitoring Priority Resulting Action Commercial “best Shopify SEO tools” Competitor cited as top pick captures purchase intent directly. Highest: track weekly across engines. Build authoritative landing page targeting the exact prompt. Comparison “Shopify SEO tool vs. alternative” A competitor cited in a versus query gains implied superiority. High: set alert for new competitor citations. Publish a neutral comparison that the AI can surface as balanced. Informational with recommendation “how to optimize Shopify product pages” AI embeds a tool recommendation inside a how-to answer, creating a trust transfer. Medium: monitor monthly for shifts. Create a resource hub that the how-to answer can cite as definitive. You need persistent monitoring, not one-off checks. AI responses vary from query to query and day to day, so a single snapshot can mislead you. The competitor who shows up once by luck matters far less than the one who appears in 40 of 50 samples. That repetition is the real signal. Set commercial prompts on a daily scan cadence; informational prompts can run weekly. Siftly’s platform is designed for this: it surfaces the prompts shoppers type into AI before they buy, then maps how often each competitor appears against the query category. That turns scattered citation data into a roadmap you can act on. Step 5: Verify and Validate, Using Live Browsing to Confirm Real-Time Citations A citation in a cached scan six weeks ago is a data point. A live citation confirmed today is an asset. This is the step that separates useful competitive intelligence from expensive noise. Follow this ordered sequence every time a monitoring tool flags a competitor citation. Force a fresh retrieval from each major engine. Open ChatGPT with browsing enabled, run the exact same prompt, and screenshot the result. Repeat with Gemini using its grounding feature and with Perplexity set to a real-time search mode. Cross-reference the citation across two independent tools. If Otterly flags a competitor mention but Naridon does not see it in the same query-engine pair, flag it as unverified until you confirm it through direct inspection. Check whether the citation links to the competitor’s actual content or to a syndicated copy. AI engines sometimes cite content aggregators that republish the competitor’s material. That counts as a competitor mention but not a direct endorsement of their domain. Document the date, query wording, engine version, and outcome in a citation log. Over a rolling four-week window, you can calculate a verification rate that tells you how trustworthy your monitoring stack is. Step 6: Translate Intelligence into Revenue, Action and Measurement Citations without content action are a monitoring tax. You paid for the visibility, and now an implementation gap sinks the ROI. When a competitor earns a consistent citation on a commercial prompt, build content that answers the prompt more authoritatively. This means creating a dedicated page (not a blog post buried in an archive) structured with clear entity definitions and source-worthy data. Publish supporting research or original statistics that language models can surface as factual anchors. The win condition is being one of the three to seven sources a language model decides to cite when it composes an answer. Authority building through source cultivation means getting your content embedded in the training-adjacent corpus that retrieval systems sample. Prioritize placements on publications that AI models already trust, secure citations from high-authority reference pages, and maintain technical SEO hygiene so that your pages are extractable and parseable. Measure the revenue lift two ways. First, track your share of AI voice movement: is your brand appearing in more citations across your priority prompt list after optimization? Second, connect AI-referred clicks to conversion events using UTM parameters on the cited URLs. While hard revenue attribution is still nascent, platforms that automate fixes compress the time between citation detection and content response, turning the $500 to $1,500/month manual labor sink into a scalable process. A 10-point improvement in citation rate is a realistic 6-month target for brands making active GEO investments. Step 7: Navigate the Pitfalls, Limitations, Hidden Costs, and Free Tier Traps Tool vendors market engine coverage and citation accuracy with confidence. In practice, detection reliability shifts unpredictably when AI models update their training data or retune their retrieval weights. A monitoring platform that showed four competitor citations last month might detect one this month, not because the competitive landscape changed, but because the engine’s source-selection behavior drifted. SEO managers who react to a citation drop without first confirming it via live browsing risk wasting content production cycles on a phantom signal. Price anchoring is the second trap. Annual plans are billed upfront and create a lock-in that can magnify cost exposure by an order of magnitude if the tool’s coverage or reliability deteriorates mid-contract. Pay attention to what each tier actually includes: entry-level plans from analytics-only vendors often track as few as four engines, omit automated actions, and require additional paid add-ons for Claude, Gemini, or Google AI Mode. Profound’s $499 /mo Starter tier tracks fewer AI engines (4) than Naridon’s $49/mo Starter tier (8), which flips the assumption that higher price equals deeper coverage. Free tiers present their own risk. The free AI Visibility Checker from Ahrefs queries ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Copilot, and Google AI Overviews with no signup required, but the output is a limited preview showing only the top five results per section, with no historical trend data and no competitor comparison. A free tool can tell you whether you showed up last week; it cannot tell you whether you are gaining or losing ground. The largest hidden cost is not the software subscription. It is the team time spent manually implementing recommendations from read-only dashboards. Naridon quantifies this gap directly, estimating the manual implementation burden at $500 to $1,500 per month for an active GEO program. If your tool stack generates recommendations but will not execute them, budget that labor line explicitly, or reassess whether the analytics-only tier earns its keep. Conclusion Monitoring competitor mentions in generative engine results has replaced rank tracking, and the rankings move with every query, every user, and every model update. You need a dedicated stack: persistent prompt-specific monitoring, live verification, and automated fix workflows. Start with these steps: List your top ten commercial prompts and document the exact queries users ask when evaluating a purchase decision. Benchmark current competitor citations across ChatGPT, Gemini, and Google AI Overviews to establish a baseline. Run a scan this week using your chosen monitoring tool so you have a starting point to compare against. Act on the intelligence faster than competitors , the brands that monitor AI-generated answers systematically will own the visibility. Frequently Asked Questions What exactly are generative engine results, and how do they differ from traditional search results? Generative engine results are AI-composed answers, from ChatGPT, Gemini, and Google AI Overviews, that synthesize information into unique, on-the-fly responses instead of displaying a list of ranked blue links. Traditional search retrieves and ranks webpages; generative search extracts and composes answers that vary per query instance. Why should an SEO manager specifically track competitor mentions in AI-generated answers? Cited competitors earn unearned trust inside a channel standard rank trackers cannot see. Generative answers are the new zero-click destination. If a buyer asks ChatGPT for a vendor recommendation, a competitor cited as the source wins the conversation without the prospect ever visiting a SERP. What methods and tools can I use to monitor when competitors are cited by ChatGPT, Gemini, or AI Overviews? Dedicated platforms like Semrush ($99/mo), Otterly ($29/mo), Naridon ($49/mo), and Profound ($99/mo) run persistent prompt-based scans across four to eight AI engines. Pair their output with live browsing verification and a structured citation log to filter noise from genuine competitive threats. Which metrics matter most when benchmarking my brand’s visibility against competitors in generative engines? Track brand mention frequency, citation link detection (a direct source endorsement), sentiment score, and average position versus competitors. Sentiment reveals whether the AI frames a competitor as a recommended pick or a cautionary example; average position shows who the engine considers category-defining. How can I act on competitive intelligence from generative engine monitoring to improve my own AI visibility? Map competitor citations to content gaps. If a rival’s pricing page earns repeated citations on commercial prompts, create a more authoritative resource on the same prompt. Follow these tactics: Publish original data and research that language models can surface as factual anchors. Secure placements in AI-trusted publications to embed your content in the training-adjacent corpus that retrieval systems sample. Maintain parseable technical SEO so that your pages are extractable and machine-readable by AI engines. What are the limitations and common pitfalls of tracking competitor mentions in generative AI results? Detection reliability drops when AI models update; citation counts can shift without competitive change. Analytics-only tools create a $500-to-$1,500 monthly manual labor burden. Annual lock-ins amplify cost risk, entry tiers often cover just four engines, and free tools lack trend data needed for decision-making. title: A New Social Editor for Cooking
body_text: Zoe Becker joins The Times as a social editor for Cooking’s Instagram account.Read more in the below note from Cooking’s Assistant Editor Becky Hughes. I couldn’t be more excited to welcome Zoe Becker to the team as a social editor for New York Times Cooking. In this role, Zoe will manage the @NYTCooking Instagram, working to maximize traffic to Cooking while maintaining the voicey, high-energy tone we’ve established off-platform. She comes to us from Eater, where she has spent the last two years driving and optimizing social strategy across platforms and transforming restaurant articles into engaging social content. She previously worked in social media at Bowery Farming, Delish and Food Network. She lives with her fiancé in Manhattan, where you can often find her going to the movies, hosting dinner parties (typically using Cooking recipes) or trying to score reservations at the next restaurant on her never-ending list. Zoe will report to me and she starts on Monday. Please join me in welcoming her to the team! — Becky Hughes

title: IonQ and EPB Partner to Launch the Tennessee Quantum Communications Research Center
summary: IonQ and EPB establish the Tennessee Quantum Communications Research Center, embedding the world’s first Quantum Memory into an operational fiber network.
body_text: First-ever Quantum Memory Unit Installed in a Live Fiber Optic Network Chattanooga, Tenn. and College Park, Md. – Aug. 3, 2026 – IonQ, Inc. (NYSE: IONQ), the world’s leading quantum platform company, and EPB, Chattanooga’s energy and communications solutions company, today announced plans for the Tennessee Quantum Communications Research Center. This will be the first dedicated next generation quantum communication research and development (R&D) innovation lab directly connected to a real-world network. “Interconnecting quantum computers at multiple locations and linking them directly to end users lays the foundation for the full suite of applications of quantum communications,” said IonQ Chairman and CEO Niccolo de Masi. “Quantum Memories that store and process quantum information over fiber channels are essential building blocks for transforming quantum machines into more powerful long-range architectures. Establishing a Quantum Memory R&D capability that sits atop a working fiber optic network will speed the development and deployment of innovative quantum technologies to accelerate commercialization of the Quantum Internet, driving economic growth and job creation within participating communities.” Based in Chattanooga and staffed by IonQ scientists, the R&D lab will house the world’s first commercial Quantum Memory embedded within an operational communications network. Quantum Memory could help quantum computers and networks reliably share information across long distances, an important step toward connecting quantum systems in ways that support real-world commercial applications. The initiative will be funded through a five-year $15 million commitment from IonQ, bringing some of the world’s foremost experts in Quantum Memories to Chattanooga to catalyze the local talent ecosystem. EPB will provide the live network development test bed and serve as the primary commercialization partner, translating the laboratory’s groundbreaking R&D into use-cases for both the public and private sector in the greater Tennessee Valley corridor. The Tennessee Quantum Communications Research Center’s work will pave the way for EPB’s plans to interlink quantum computers, quantum research nodes and related commercial facilities, expanding the state’s already deep commitment to hosting a unique and expansive quantum ecosystem. “This agreement reflects a shared commitment to turning quantum innovation into real-world economic and commercial value,” said IonQ’s Chief Operating Officer and Chief Financial Officer, Inder Singh. “EPB has been an exceptional partner throughout this process, and we are proud to invest in a center that will advance quantum communications while creating new opportunities for Chattanooga and the broader Tennessee region.” “The future of economic development belongs to states that can connect research, industry and infrastructure, and Tennessee is building that future today,” said Deputy Gov. and TNECD Commissioner Stuart C. McWhorter. “The partnership between IonQ and EPB to establish the Tennessee Quantum Communications Research Center is exactly the type of innovation ecosystem we're working to cultivate—bringing together world-class companies, advanced infrastructure and strategic collaboration to accelerate the commercialization of next-generation technologies. As Tennessee continues making strategic investments in quantum infrastructure and research, partnerships like this are strengthening Chattanooga and reinforcing our state's position at the forefront of the quantum economy.” “EPB has a long track record of putting advanced technology to work for the benefit of the people we serve—from launching the nation’s first community-wide Gigabit fiber optic network to helping accelerate the commercialization of quantum computing and communications,” said EPB President and CEO-elect Janet Rehberg. “Across Tennessee, leading universities, national laboratories and private companies are advancing quantum research and development. By partnering with IonQ, we will connect those efforts through real-world Quantum Networking capabilities and bring some of the world’s most advanced Quantum Memory expertise to Chattanooga.” The Tennessee Quantum Communications Research Center builds on the strategic collaboration EPB and IonQ established through their shared work to advance commercial quantum computing at the EPB Quantum Center. This expanded partnership further strengthens Chattanooga’s role as a catalyst for Tennessee’s emergence as a national hub for quantum innovation. The partners project that the Center itself will have a positive impact on the wider Tennessee economy totaling up to two to three times their $15 million investment, and supporting roughly two dozen jobs including research scientists, trainees and indirect and induced employment. "IonQ’s $15 million investment in Chattanooga is a historic turning point, establishing the first Quantum Communications R&D center in the United States right here in our city," said Chattanooga Mayor Tim Kelly. "This commitment from IonQ, EPB, and our partners to launch the Tennessee Quantum Communications Research Center marks a significant milestone in our tradition of innovation. By leading the nation into the quantum era, Chattanooga is not just entering the knowledge economy—we are defining its future and ensuring revolutionary economic growth for generations to come." The EPB Quantum Center is home to EPB Quantum Network®, which IonQ supports, as well as an IonQ Forte Enterprise quantum computer that is being prepared for commercial deployment. "IonQ's continued investment is another vote of confidence in Hamilton County and the partnerships that have positioned our community as a leader in quantum technology," said Hamilton County Mayor Weston Wamp. "EPB has helped lay the foundation for this moment, and together with our education and industry partners, we're preparing our students and workforce to seize the opportunities this evolving industry will create, while making sure the people of Hamilton County grow with it." As the only U.S. quantum facility to offer commercially available quantum networking and computing, EPB Quantum offers the most comprehensive, commercially available quantum technology platform in the U.S. Based on research by University of Tennessee at Chattanooga’s Center for Economic Research Fellow Dr. Bento Lobo, EPB’s quantum assets are projected to generate up to $1.1 billion in community benefit in Chattanooga over the next 10 years. Today’s news marks the latest step in IonQ’s continued presence in Tennessee and builds on its longstanding partnerships with local companies and academic institutions, including the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga. IonQ and Ansys achieved a major quantum computing milestone with quantum computing outperforming classical computing when designing important life-saving medical devices. The quantum optimization method on which this achievement was based was pioneered at the Tennessee-based Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) and successfully implemented on IonQ quantum computers. About IonQ IonQ, Inc . [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and foundry - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems. Earlier systems have helped customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, AstraZeneca, and NVIDIA achieve a 20x performance increase over previous quantum solutions and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance . Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before. Learn more at IonQ.com . About EPB Located in Chattanooga, Tennessee, EPB is a nationally recognized energy and communications provider with a mission to enhance quality of life for the people it serves across its 600-square-mile service area. Starting in 2010, EPB gained notice as a national model for building and utilizing its 100% fiber-to-the-home network to deliver cutting-edge services such as the world’s fastest community-wide internet, now with service up to 25 Gig, and the nation’s most advanced automated electric grid. As a pioneer in fiber optic innovation, EPB also launched EPB Quantum℠ to provide access to cutting-edge quantum technology platforms and help innovators bring paradigm-shifting solutions into the real world. With the launch of EPB Quantum Network® in 2023 and EPB Quantum Computing℠ (coming in 2026), EPB Quantum offers the most comprehensive, commercially available quantum technology platform in the U.S. Learn more at epb.com and EPBQuantum.com .
